subject: history_social
passage: Viking longships, used in Scandinavia from about 800 to 1100 CE, were built for more than ocean crossings. Their hulls were remarkably ______, often sitting only about a meter deep in the water even when the ships were loaded. As a result, Viking crews could row far up rivers into the heart of Europe and run their ships right onto beaches where there was no harbor.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The hulls sat "only about a meter deep in the water," which let the ships travel up rivers and land on beaches. A hull that does not reach far below the surface is shallow, so "shallow" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A deep hull would run aground in rivers and on beaches, the opposite of what the text describes.
explanation.B: Correct. Sitting "only about a meter deep," the hulls were shallow, which let crews row up rivers and onto beaches.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A heavy, loaded ship would sink deeper into the water; the text stresses how little of the hull was below the surface.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about decoration; it explains how the hull's shape let the ships reach rivers and beaches.
